stem:
The melting points of some solids are shown in Table 1.1.

**Table 1.1**

| solid | melting point/K |
| :--- | :--- |
| magnesium | 923 |
| phosphorus | 317 |
| sodium chloride | 1074 |
| sulfur | 392 |

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State the type of bonding present in magnesium and in sodium chloride.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain the difference in the melting points of magnesium and sodium chloride.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Explain the difference in the melting points of phosphorus and sulfur in terms of structure and bonding.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why electronegativity increases across a period.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Name the strongest intermolecular force that exists between $\text{NH}_3\text{(l)}$ molecules.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
Draw a diagram to show the formation of the strongest intermolecular force between **two** molecules of $\text{NH}_3\text{(l)}$.

Include any relevant lone pairs of electrons and dipoles.

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.text:
The melting points of ice and ammonia are shown in Table 1.2.

**Table 1.2**

| solid | melting point/K |
| :--- | :--- |
| ice | 273 |
| ammonia | 195 |

Suggest **two** reasons for the difference in the melting points of ice and ammonia.
